title: ProP-PD / PDZ-Seq
reason: scope:PDZ-Seq: The poster explicitly groups PDZ-Seq with ProP-PD, and its literal PDZ-Seq reference matches Ernst et al. The supplied Ernst abstract establishes peptide-phage/deep-sequencing profiling of evolved PDZ-domain binding specificity. That supports the three separate local profiling interfaces listed here. It does not establish the natural C-terminal oligo design, the ProP-PD phage-library history or the exact plate-attachment format for that paper. Consequently none of o_identify, o_oligos, o_phages, o_select, o_sequence or o_count is reassigned to PDZ-Seq: their fixed inputs retain the ProP-PD history. Applicability of the entire grouped drawing to the historical PDZ-Seq implementation remains unresolved; shared binding-profile purpose is supported. Upstream domain evolution in the Ernst study is background input history, not another target or an extra depicted preparation branch.; correction:c_pdz_scope: The ProP-PD abstract explicitly supports the C-terminal oligo-derived library. The associated Ernst abstract supports peptide-phage/deep-sequencing specificity profiling of evolved PDZ domains but does not establish that library construction or the precise plate format. The source-supported resolution is a common profiling purpose with a member-specific local interface, while identity of the complete preparation remains unestablished; the diagram is preserved.

candidate.title: ProP-PD / PDZ-Seq
candidate.scope: Assigned lower row of the Protein-Protein Interactions poster, labeled ProP-PD / PDZ-Seq. Inventory: Protein target overview icon; Identify C-terminal sequences; Create oligo library; Construct phage display library; Bait proteins immobilized on 96-well plate; Hybridize; Select phages against baits; Isolate and sequence; Peptide counts (2 and 1). The lower row has a library route and an independently prepared immobilized-bait input converging on binding selection; it shows no split, pooling or explicit repeat loop. The Protein target line is a purpose icon, not a transferred sample. The neighboring PD-Seq row supplies no operations, chemistry or three-cycle loop to this record. The C-terminal oligo-derived route is supported for the depicted ProP-PD implementation. PDZ-Seq remains a distinct grouped target: separate local selection/sequencing/count interfaces express its paper-supported profiling purpose without assigning it ProP-PD input history. Those interfaces are an explicit interpretation of shared captions, not an additional drawn branch. Only supplied abstracts, publication metadata, the inspected diagram and the verified secondary catalogue page support factual claims; no full-text protocol or equivalence of complete implementations is claimed.

method_scopes.rationale: All six original local operations describe the depicted ProP-PD implementation: oligo-defined C-terminal peptide candidates become a phage-display library, which is selected against independently immobilized baits before encoding sequences are read and counted. The Ivarsson abstract identifies this method by name and reports custom oligo microarrays, human/viral C-terminal peptide libraries and PDZ-domain screening. The catalogue heading and caption specifically identify this schematic as ProP-PD. PDZ baits therefore fall within ProP-PD here; the names are not assumed to be aliases or interchangeable protocols. This is the assigned implementation, not a claim that every ProP-PD library has the same preparation.

research_questions.question: The poster explicitly groups PDZ-Seq with ProP-PD, and its literal PDZ-Seq reference matches Ernst et al. The supplied Ernst abstract establishes peptide-phage/deep-sequencing profiling of evolved PDZ-domain binding specificity. That supports the three separate local profiling interfaces listed here. It does not establish the natural C-terminal oligo design, the ProP-PD phage-library history or the exact plate-attachment format for that paper. Consequently none of o_identify, o_oligos, o_phages, o_select, o_sequence or o_count is reassigned to PDZ-Seq: their fixed inputs retain the ProP-PD history. Applicability of the entire grouped drawing to the historical PDZ-Seq implementation remains unresolved; shared binding-profile purpose is supported. Upstream domain evolution in the Ernst study is background input history, not another target or an extra depicted preparation branch.

The ProP-PD abstract explicitly supports the C-terminal oligo-derived library. The associated Ernst abstract supports peptide-phage/deep-sequencing specificity profiling of evolved PDZ domains but does not establish that library construction or the precise plate format. The source-supported resolution is a common profiling purpose with a member-specific local interface, while identity of the complete preparation remains unestablished; the diagram is preserved.
